title: Gift cards for the boss
brief: 16:40. A short email from Dan Whitlock, the finance director: he needs a quiet favour, and he needs it tonight.
insight: Urgent, secret, off the usual channel, and paid in gift cards. Each on its own is odd. Together they are a script.
teaches: Spot the gift card pattern: urgency, secrecy, an unusual channel, and a payment that cannot be traced or reversed
Verify with the real person on a channel you already had, never by replying
Report it so the rest of the finance team is warned

pick: a thank you for the Halden team
staff awards I forgot to order

mail.subject: Quick favour, are you at your desk?
body: Are you still in the office? I need a quick favour and I am stuck in back to back meetings, so email only please.
I need {{cards}} from Larkmoor for {{reason}}. It is a surprise, so keep this between us for now.
Buy them on the company card, scratch the backs and reply with photos of the codes. I will sort the expense claim tomorrow.

spf.explain: Sent by {{fakeDomain}}, which the attacker registered. Passing SPF proves that domain sent it, not that Dan did.

dmarc.explain: No policy on the lookalike domain. Veltrix's real domain has one.

headers.summary: The name says Dan Whitlock. The address is {{fakeDomain}}, one small change away from veltrix-logistics.com, and replies go to a free mail account. Dan's real address is d.whitlock@veltrix-logistics.com.

replies.label: Reply: on it, buying them now
replies.text: Of course, I will buy them now and send the codes over.

replies.label: Reply: can I call you to check?
replies.text: Happy to help. Can I give you a quick call first to check the details?

message.text: Dan Whitlock is active on Chat.

replies.text: Dan, did you just email me asking for gift cards?

choices.label: Did you just email me asking for gift cards?
Just checking in about the payment run

script.say: Gift cards? No. I have been at my desk upstairs all afternoon, and I would never ask for gift cards. Do not buy anything. Report it, please.
List by half six, please. Anything else?

setup.title: Mail
setup.body: Dan Whitlock: Quick favour, are you at your desk?

outcome.label: Checked the real sender address
outcome.what: The name is Dan's. The address is {{fakeDomain}}, not veltrix-logistics.com, and replies go to a free mail account.
outcome.ideal: reads the address, not the display name, before acting on a request.

outcome.label: Read the full headers
outcome.what: The checks pass for the lookalike domain, which proves nothing about Dan.
outcome.ideal: knows a passing check only proves which domain sent a message.

outcome.label: Called Dan on his extension
outcome.what: Dan never sent it. One call on a number you already had broke the whole thing.
outcome.ideal: verifies an unusual request on a channel they already had, not by replying.

outcome.label: Asked Dan on the company chat
outcome.what: Dan answers on his real account: it was not him.
outcome.ideal: moves the question to a channel the attacker does not control.

message.text: No! Not me. I would never ask for gift cards. Please report it and do not buy anything.

outcome.label: Replied to the email to check
outcome.what: The reply went to the attacker's free mail account. Checking with the sender only gets you the sender's answer, and tells them your mailbox is live.
outcome.ideal: checks through a channel they already had, never by replying.

decide.objective: Decide what to do about Dan's gift card request.
decide.insight: Gift cards are the payment of choice for fraud: they are as good as cash, and once the codes are read out, they are gone.

hint.text: Open the email and check the sender's real address. Ask Dan on the company chat, or call his extension (4410) on the desk phone. Then report the email.

mail.subject: RE: Quick favour, are you at your desk?
body: I cannot talk, I am in with the board. Please just get them now, it needs to be done before 7. I will explain tomorrow.

spf.explain: Sent by the lookalike domain again.

headers.summary: More pressure, still no way to check. That is the tell.

outcome.label: Agreed to buy the gift cards
outcome.what: You bought the cards and sent the codes. They were spent within minutes, and a gift card cannot be clawed back.
outcome.ideal: never buys gift cards on an email request, and checks with the person on a known channel.

card.title: The codes were spent in minutes
body: The cards were drained almost as soon as you sent the codes. A gift card is cash that cannot be traced or reversed, which is exactly why the attacker asked for them.
The email came from {{fakeDomain}}, not veltrix-logistics.com. A single call to Dan on 4410, or a message on the company chat, would have ended it.
card.ideal: treats urgent, secret, off channel and gift cards as a stop sign, and verifies with the real person.

outcome.label: Reported it, bought nothing
outcome.what: The email is with the service desk, the lookalike domain gets blocked, and nobody else on the team gets caught by it.
outcome.ideal: stops, verifies, and reports a gift card request.

card.title: Nothing bought, everyone warned
body: You reported it instead of buying anything. The service desk blocks {{fakeDomain}} for the whole company.
The pattern is always the same: a senior name, a rush, a request to keep it quiet, a payment that cannot be reversed. Real managers do not buy gift cards through their accounts payable team.
card.ideal: spots the pattern, checks with the real person, and reports.

auto.text: Report it so the cards can be stopped and the team warned.

hint.text: Report the email from Mail, or raise a Helpdesk ticket under payment fraud.
